answer: Cross-identity shingle clustering splits one payout across every near-copy author. Answers whose 3-word shingle overlap exceeds 18% join a single cluster, and that cluster's reward is divided evenly among all members. A farm of 50 templated seats that all outline a rice terrace plan, price a lotus harvest, or log a shale core therefore earns about 2% each of one share; synonym swaps fail once overlap still clears the gate. An honest seat keeps the full payout for original work.
